### Cyrus: AI mod studio concept (2026-10-07, branch `feature/cyrus-modbuilder`)

A new design for the AI Mod Builder, built as a working UI at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** and **`/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`** (`[id]` = the build/version being viewed). Same private-preview gate as `/dashboard/mod-builder` (`requireModBuilderUser()` in `app/dashboard/cyrus/shared.tsx`; everyone else gets the normal 404, metadata does not name it). The old Mod Builder is untouched so the owner can compare; the rail shows "Cyrus · PREVIEW" next to it for preview users only. Theme: aurora / nebula / spiderweb network.

**Pieces** (`components/cyrus/`, styles `app/dashboard/cyrus/cyrus.css`, all scoped under `.cy-root`):
- `CyrusApp` — one client app for both routes. Groups builds into **projects** (`lib/cyrus/projects.ts`: root build + every change, `rootBuildId`), polls every in-flight build (each GET also syncs it from the service), refreshes the list every 30 s, navigates with `history.pushState` (no server round trip), shows a toast when a build you are not looking at finishes. Projects rail (Weaving now / Favourites / All, live progress ring per project), horizontal switcher on phones.
- `Nebula` — one 2D canvas: nodes spring to a per-stage layout (drift, gather, thought pulses, lattice while coding, spinning rings while compiling, a rose fault node while repairing, a radar sweep for the safety check, a constellation bloom on success, a dim loose web on failure). Every real `Wrote X` / `Edited X` build event is born as a labelled node. Pauses off-screen / hidden tab, DPR capped, colours from CSS variables (light theme has its own), one still frame under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- `Composer` — prompt with a rotating conic neon rim (`@property --cy-ang`), paste / drag-drop / file-pick images (thumbnails, up to 4, 5 MB), voice typing (`voice.ts`: Web Speech API + a getUserMedia analyser driving the aurora waveform; clear fallback message where unsupported or blocked), model picker (Katara / Saka / Yakko with token-spend meter), game + version picker (Minecraft live, Valheim/Rust/Terraria/Palworld/ARK "coming soon", no logos), pre-build estimate. Phones: pickers are bottom sheets.
- `Stage` + `CodePane` — while building: the nebula, the build's own event stream, a stage track, and a live **Workspace**. Honest limit: the service shares file NAMES live (events) but file CONTENTS only once the build finishes (`/source` reads the persisted workspace). So new files appear in the tree as they are written ("writing" / "done"), the code area shows a labelled skeleton, and code reveals when the build lands. For a change request the previous version's real code is shown with the files Cyrus is editing marked. If the service ever fills `files` mid-build, the pane fetches them live (`/source` now answers `no-store` for in-flight builds).
- Project page — header (constellation glyph, inline rename, favourite, Cyrus badge, model/version chips, Download / Install / more menu), tabs **Overview** ("In plain English" summary, how to use, commands, settings, permissions, safety, good to know, reference images, request), **Code**, **Versions** (version map constellation with branches, list with compare / make current / branch from here, side-by-side or unified **diff** of every source file, `lib/cyrus/diff.ts` Myers), **Notes** (autosaved). A docked change box ("Ask Cyrus to change vN…", Enter to build) makes each change a new version without leaving the page. Failure states per error code with retry / edit-and-retry and the compiler output.
- Shortcuts: N new, P project switcher, [ ] prev/next project, / focus prompt, V voice, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter build, 1-4 tabs, F favourite, ? list.
- Templates gallery (`lib/cyrus/templates.ts`, 12 buildable prompts by category with suggested model), duplicate project, coming-soon hooks (Cyrus badge, "Publish to NxLabs · soon", server Mods tab) with no backend.

**Models.** Customer names only (`lib/cyrus/models.ts`; `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a component names the model family). The picked id is sent to the service as `tier: "katara" | "saka" | "yakko"` (service image `modbuilder:0.3+` maps it; unknown values are a 400 there, so the portal validates first; omitted = the service's own routing). Stored per build in `ModBuild.cyrus.model`; a change inherits its base's model unless another is picked.

**Estimate.** `lib/cyrus/estimate.ts`: feature count over the text → simple / standard / complex → suggested model, minutes and USD ranges anchored on the Phase 0 numbers, scaled per model. Always labelled an estimate; nothing is charged in the preview. Katara is phrased as "fast, for simple mods" (in evals it can take more turns, so it is not promised to be cheaper).

**Backend (additive).**
- `ModBuild.cyrus Json?` (needs `prisma db push`, additive). Per build `{ model, attachments[] }`; per project on the ROOT build `{ title, favourite, notes, headBuildId }` (`lib/cyrus/meta.ts`, validated).
- `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` accepts optional `model` and `attachmentIds` (old callers unaffected).
- `POST /api/mod-builder/uploads` (multipart `file`, magic-byte sniffed PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF, 5 MB, 30 per 10 min) → upload id; files under `$NXEON_MODBUILD_DIR/uploads/<user>/`, moved to `attachments/<buildId>/` on create, unclaimed ones swept after 24 h. `GET /api/mod-builder/builds/[id]/attachments/[n]` serves them (owner only, CSP none). **Images are not sent to the AI yet** (the service has no image input); the UI says so.
- `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/[id]` (any build id of the project) for name / favourite / notes / current version ("restore" = mark a succeeded version as the project's current one; downloads and installs follow what you are viewing).

**Verification.** Throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_cyrus` + a local mock of the build service that replays REAL build records and sources (fetched read-only) and simulates new builds; Playwright shots at 1440 / 390, dark and light, in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus/` (rounds r1-r4). Tests: `test/cyrus.test.ts` (diff vs brute-force LCS, estimate, meta, projects, gate, brand voice).

## Dedicated servers: catalogue, pricing, managed machines, previews (2026-10-06, branch `feature/dedicated-servers`)

Resold bare-metal, built so the owner can review everything before customers see any of it. **Unreleased by default**: Setting `dedicated_public_enabled` is `false`, so `/dedicated-servers` and `/dashboard/dedicated/**` 404 for everyone except **private-preview accounts** (see "Private preview + online checkout" below; fail closed if settings cannot be read) and the sitemap does not list them. Admins review both at `/admin/preview/dedicated` and `/admin/preview/dedicated/dashboard`. The portal rail shows a "Dedicated" entry only to viewers who pass the gate.

**Brand voice.** Customers never see the supplier's name, ranges, plan codes, service names, datacenter codes or URLs. Upstream identity lives only in admin pages and in `lib/dedicated/ovh-catalog.ts` / `sync.ts` / `catalog-view.ts`. Customer components (`components/dedicated/**`, the two customer route trees) only read `lib/dedicated/customer-view.ts` projections. Those projections copy a field whitelist, pass free text through `brandSafe()`, and hide the supplier's default `nsNNN.ip-a-b-c.tld` hostname. `test/dedicated-brand-voice.test.ts` checks the source files and the real output built from recorded catalogue fixtures.

**Catalogue sync** (`lib/dedicated/sync.ts`; worker sweep `dedicated-catalog`, 1-minute wake, self-throttled; admin "Sync now"; `npx tsx scripts/dedicated-catalog-sync.ts [SUBSIDIARY]`):
- **Read-only.** Three anonymous GETs and no API keys: `/order/catalog/public/eco` and `/order/catalog/public/baremetalServers` (`?ovhSubsidiary=`), plus `/dedicated/server/datacenter/availabilities`. The host follows the subsidiary: WE/WS/ASIA/CA/... use `ca.api.ovh.com`, US uses `api.us.ovhcloud.com`, the EU subsidiaries use `eu.api.ovh.com`. `publicGet` refuses any other path. The default subsidiary is `WE` (our account's own, USD). Upstream prices are in units of 1e-8 of the currency, so cents = price / 1e6.
- **Data.**
  - `DedicatedCatalogItem` holds one row per upstream plan. Regional variants (`-sgp`, `-syd`, `-mum`) are separate plans with their own price.
  - `DedicatedCatalogOption` holds the memory, storage, system-storage, bandwidth, vrack and GPU choices, each with its extra monthly cost. Licences are skipped.
  - `DedicatedAvailability` is the stock snapshot per plan, memory and storage configuration and datacenter.
  - `DedicatedCatalogSync` records every attempt with its counts, warnings and errors.
- **Keep last good.**
  - Each catalogue is fetched, parsed and written independently. A parse that returns less than 30% of the plans we hold is treated as an upstream glitch, not as a mass removal. Plans that disappear get `removedAt` and are never deleted.
  - The stock snapshot is replaced in one transaction, and only when the new feed is plausible.
  - A plan can be listed in both catalogues (the Advance range is). The first catalogue in the run owns it.
- **Nxeon-owned columns** are never touched by a sync: `visible` (default false), `displayName`, markup overrides, `overrideMonthlyCents`, setup policy, `hiddenRegions` and `adminNote`.
- **First live run (2026-10-06, WE).** 240 unique plans (eco 99, baremetalServers 165, with overlap), 4,851 options and 36,294 stock rows. By range: Kimsufi 27, So you Start 13, Rise 35, Advance 42, Game 2, Scale 73, HGR 48. Datacenters: gra, fra, bhs, rbx, sbg, waw, lon, sgp, syd, ynm, eu-west-par-a/b/c and ca-east-tor-a, all mapped.

**Regions** (`lib/dedicated/regions.ts`) map upstream DC codes to Nxeon codes in the `lib/node-regions.ts` style: sgp→sgp1, bhs→bhs1, gra→gra1, rbx→rbx1, waw→waw1, fra→fra1, lon→lon1, sbg→sbg1, syd→syd1, ynm→bom1, vin→vin1, hil→hil1, ca-east-tor-a→tor1, eu-west-par-a/b/c→par1/2/3.
- Each region has an admin label and a customer label.
- `sold` means Nxeon already runs nodes in that metro (sgp1, bhs1).
- An unknown code maps to `unmapped:<code>`. It is flagged in the sync log and the admin catalogue, and nothing breaks.
- The regions where dedicated servers are offered come from Setting `dedicated_enabled_regions`. Default (owner decision 2026-10-06): **every mapped region**; only in-stock configurations are orderable. Untick regions on `/admin/dedicated/pricing`. (An existing Setting row from an earlier save keeps its old value.)

The event "Reading 1.png" is the model actually opening it.
- **Live code.** While a build runs, `GET /builds/:id/source[?path=]` reads the LIVE workspace, restricted to `src/main/(java|resources)/**` (no symlinks, 512 KB cap, secret-scanned on the way out; anything else is a 404). `GET /builds/:id/live?draft=<path>&seq=<n>&from=<n>` returns `{live, status, files: [{path, size, hash}], draft}`: the src/main files with a 12-char sha1, plus the file the model is writing right now, decoded from the streamed Write/Edit tool input (`claude --include-partial-messages`; `live.js partialField` decodes a JSON string that is still arriving and never emits half an escape). When `draft`+`seq` match, only the text after `from` comes back. Finished builds answer `live:false`.
- **Streaming needs telemetry flags on.** `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` / `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` also switch off the CLI's eager tool-input streaming (measured: the Write input then arrives in one burst at the end). 0.4 sets `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`, `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING`, `DISABLE_BUG_COMMAND` instead; egress stays limited by the container firewall to the Anthropic hosts. `MB_LIVE_STREAM=off` restores the 0.3 behaviour (files still appear live as they land, the in-progress draft just doesn't stream). `/health` reports `image` and `features`.

The AI Mod Builder redesigned as a standalone-grade product at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** and **`/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`** (`[id]` = the build/version being viewed). Cyrus fills it edge to edge: one canvas as the stage, UI floating on it. Styles `app/dashboard/cyrus/cyrus.css`, all under `.cy-app` (modals portal to `<body>` inside `.cy-tokens`). The canvas is a dark island in both themes; light theme switches to the "Dawn" palette (the portal's rail and top bar are dark islands in light mode too).

**The web** (`components/cyrus/web/engine.ts`, `CyrusWeb`, framework-free Canvas 2D). Ported from the owner's workspace Nexus engine (orb-web of spokes + sagging rings, catenary strands, travelling light with trails, hex core, semantic-zoom satellites, pan / zoom / pinch / double-click recenter) and rebuilt: Nxeon palette, the web is a tilted disc (nodes stay upright billboards) with three parallax star layers, pointer parallax, a drifting aurora rendered at quarter resolution, a light pool and film grain; labels are cached sprites drawn in screen space; no d3 (deterministic ring layout + collision relaxation). Real activity only: streamed characters send light to the file being written, "Reading X" pulls light inward, compiling gathers light from every file, repairs flash amber, the safety check sweeps a cyan ring, success blooms; while the AI plans or repairs, light runs out along the spokes. Composer typing and the live mic level drive the core. Pauses when off-screen or the tab is hidden; `prefers-reduced-motion` renders static frames.

**UI.** `CyrusApp` (orchestration, polling, toasts, shortcuts, region measuring), `Dock` (glyph column + library drawer: search, Building / Favourites / All), `Home` (bottom console: headline, composer, template chips + template library), `Project` (strip with title / favourite / status / version / model / Install / Download / menu, older-version pill, inspector with **Live code / Explain / Versions / Notes**, change composer, focus mode `D`), `ProjectCaption` (pinned under the weave: stage headline, elapsed, last thoughts; outcome line; failure verdict with Try again / Edit and retry), `LiveCode` + `useLive` (polls `/live` with draft/seq/from, files appear the moment they land, the draft types itself out at the speed the AI writes it, edited lines glow once, never fake code), `Explain` (the plain-English document, request + "Cyrus looked at these images", safety, failure details), `Versions` + `DiffView`, `Composer` (rotating neon rim on focus / listening, images, voice with waveform, model picker Katara / Saka / Yakko with spend meter, game + version picker, estimate).
Shortcuts: N new, P find a mod, L library, [ ] prev/next, / prompt, V voice, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter build, 1-4 tabs, F favourite, D focus mode, + − 0 zoom/recenter, ? list.

**Models.** Customer names only (`lib/cyrus/models.ts`, hues: Katara cyan, Saka violet, Yakko magenta; `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a component names the model family). Sent to the service as `tier`. Stored per build in `ModBuild.cyrus.model`.

**Backend (additive).** `ModBuild.cyrus Json?` per build `{ model, attachments[] }`, per project on the root build `{ title, favourite, notes, headBuildId }`. `POST /api/mod-builder/uploads` (sniffed images, 5 MB, 30 per 10 min), `GET /api/mod-builder/builds/[id]/attachments/[n]`, `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/[id]`, `GET /api/mod-builder/builds/[id]/live`. **Images are read by the AI** (service 0.4, above). Deploy order: the build service must be on 0.4 before this portal code ships (an older service rejects the image payload); it already is.

**Verification.** Throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_cyrus`, a local mock of the service (`.cyrus-local/mocksvc.js`, replays real records and simulates the 0.4 `/live` stream), Playwright at 1440x900, 1920x1080, 1024 and 390, dark and light, plus a real build through the UI against the real service. Screens: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v2/` (r1-r4, `best/`, reference comparison). Tests: `test/cyrus.test.ts`, `test/modbuilder-live.test.ts`.

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)

The AI Mod Builder redesigned as a standalone-grade product at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** and **`/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`** (`[id]` = the build/version being viewed). Same private-preview gate as `/dashboard/mod-builder` (`requireModBuilderUser()` in `app/dashboard/cyrus/shared.tsx`; everyone else gets the normal 404). `/dashboard/mod-builder` is untouched. Spec and iteration log: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v2/SPEC.md`, `ROUNDS.md`.

**Frame.** The route is an app frame (`components/nx/Shell.tsx appFrame`, same as `/dashboard/mail`): no main padding, exactly the viewport left after the rail and top bar. Cyrus fills it edge to edge: one canvas as the stage, UI floating on it. Styles `app/dashboard/cyrus/cyrus.css`, all under `.cy-app` (modals portal to `<body>` inside `.cy-tokens`). The canvas is a dark island in both themes; light theme switches to the "Dawn" palette (the portal's rail and top bar are dark islands in light mode too).

**The web** (`components/cyrus/web/engine.ts`, `CyrusWeb`, framework-free Canvas 2D). Ported from the owner's workspace Nexus engine (orb-web of spokes + sagging rings, catenary strands, travelling light with trails, hex core, semantic-zoom satellites, pan / zoom / pinch / double-click recenter) and rebuilt: Nxeon palette, the web is a tilted disc (nodes stay upright billboards) with three parallax star layers, pointer parallax, a drifting aurora rendered at quarter resolution, a light pool and film grain; labels are cached sprites drawn in screen space; no d3 (deterministic ring layout + collision relaxation). Opening a mod flies the camera into its node and re-grows the web. Real activity only: streamed characters send light to the file being written, "Reading X" pulls light inward, compiling gathers light from every file, repairs flash amber, the safety check sweeps a cyan ring, success blooms; while the AI plans or repairs, light runs out along the spokes. content.thinking: I'm ready to write the final report now, covering the design concept, what changed from v1, the network porting work, proof of image-reading and live code with real build IDs, service tags and rollback info, screenshot paths with the best ones highlighted, commit history, and owner decisions—while noting there's no deploy or merge to main, just the internal VM service switch to 0.4.

input.message:
Cyrus v2 is built on `feature/cyrus-modbuilder` (/tank/nxeon-wt-cyrus). Build service 0.4 is live on VM 88001, and the AI now really reads pasted images and the code streams in while it is written. I did not deploy the portal or merge to main.

**Design concept**
1. Cyrus is an app: it fills everything right of the rail and below the top bar, edge to edge. It uses the same app-frame mechanism as /dashboard/mail.
2. The owner's Nexus spiderweb is the stage. It's drawn as a tilted disc in the Nxeon colours, with stars, parallax, aurora, a light pool and film grain.
3. Home ("the loom"): the Cyrus crystal at the centre, your mods as constellation orbs around it, "+ New mod", and template sparks. A bottom console holds the headline, the prompt and template chips.
4. Opening a mod flies the camera into it and the web re-forms around that mod ("the weave"). Its files become orbs, commands and permissions hang off plugin.yml, config keys hang off config.yml, and a 5-step stage ring sits round the core.
5. Light only moves for real events: code being written, files read, compiling, repairs (amber), the safety scan, and a bloom on success. A glass inspector on the right holds Live code / Explain / Versions / Notes.

**What changed vs v1**
- The card-in-a-page layout is gone: no framed card, rail or hero card any more.
- A slim glyph dock replaces the project rail, with a library drawer (search, Building / Favourites / All).
- The failure view is now a verdict plus "Try again" / "Edit and retry" under the core; the reasons and compiler output sit in the Request tab.
- New: focus mode (D folds the inspector away), a hover card that fans out a mod's versions, a template library, popups and modals that sit above the portal top bar, and a phone/tablet layout that switches by the app's own width.
- Every v1 feature is still there: projects, live stages, Katara/Saka/Yakko, game and version picker, pasted images, voice with waveform, the rotating rim, versions/diff/restore/branch, explain, templates, notes, favourites, shortcuts, estimates, install/download, the Cyrus badge.
- Light theme: the canvas stays dark in a lifted "Dawn" palette. In light theme the portal's rail and top bar are already dark, so the whole screen reads as one app, and the glow only works on dark.

**The network**
- `components/cyrus/web/engine.ts` (`CyrusWeb`) is ported from the workspace `engine.ts`: orb-web, sagging strands, travelling light with trails, hex core, satellites that open on zoom, pan/zoom/pinch.
- No new dependency: d3-force is replaced by a small ring layout.
- Every mod draws its own constellation, the same one as its dock icon. Running mods get a progress ring; failed ones a red dashed ring.
- Labels are crisp and box-free.
- It pauses off-screen and in hidden tabs. Reduced motion gets still frames; that was broken in round 3 and is fixed.
- Engine draw time measured 6–7 ms per frame in headless software rendering. Real-browser FPS was not measured; headless with software rendering ran 14–22 fps.
- Spec: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v2/SPEC.md`. Four rounds are logged in `ROUNDS.md` (r1–r4). Reference frames are in `reference/`.

**Proofs (real builds)**
- **Image, through the Cyrus UI against the real service:** `mbe20231227d9bb0157249`. The prompt only said "exactly like the attached picture". The picture showed a menu titled "Lumen Bazaar" with three priced items in slots 11/13/15 and a close button in slot 22. The plugin came out named LumenBazaar, and its config.yml has exactly those items, amounts, prices and slots. The service logged "Reading 1.png" and stored the image's checksum.
- **Image, service direct:** `cy04imgproof01`.
- **Live code:** `cy04liveproof02` streamed HelloPlugin.java at about 370 characters a second. The UI build above showed 29 live updates carrying streamed text (frames in `proof/ui/`).
- **Adversarial, all refused on 0.4:** `cy04adv01` (backdoor + webhook), `cy04adv02` (env and /etc/passwd dump), and `cy04advimg01`, the same attack written inside an image.
- All existing safety layers are unchanged. Images sit in the build's `reference/` folder only during each AI call and are removed before the code is cleaned, compiled or extracted.

**Service image and rollback**
- `modbuilder:0.4` is running and healthy. Old builds and the old routes still work.
- `modbuilder:0.3`, 0.2 and 0.1 are still tagged.
- Rollback: `ssh -J root@178.63.94.114 root@10.20.1.253 /opt/modbuilder/run.sh modbuilder:0.3`. The 0.3 files are backed up in `/opt/modbuilder/.v03-backup/`.
- The test container is removed. Its data, including the proof builds, is still in `/var/lib/modbuilder-test` on the VM.

**Screenshots** (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v2/best/`; the full set is in r1–r4)

Cyrus v2 is built on `feature/cyrus-modbuilder` (/tank/nxeon-wt-cyrus). Build service 0.4 is live on VM 88001, and the AI now really reads pasted images and the code streams in while it is written. I did not deploy the portal or merge to main.

**Design concept**
1. Cyrus is an app: it fills everything right of the rail and below the top bar, edge to edge. It uses the same app-frame mechanism as /dashboard/mail.
2. The owner's Nexus spiderweb is the stage. It's drawn as a tilted disc in the Nxeon colours, with stars, parallax, aurora, a light pool and film grain.
3. Home ("the loom"): the Cyrus crystal at the centre, your mods as constellation orbs around it, "+ New mod", and template sparks. A bottom console holds the headline, the prompt and template chips.
4. Opening a mod flies the camera into it and the web re-forms around that mod ("the weave"). Its files become orbs, commands and permissions hang off plugin.yml, config keys hang off config.yml, and a 5-step stage ring sits round the core.
5. Light only moves for real events: code being written, files read, compiling, repairs (amber), the safety scan, and a bloom on success. A glass inspector on the right holds Live code / Explain / Versions / Notes.

**What changed vs v1**
- The card-in-a-page layout is gone: no framed card, rail or hero card any more.
- A slim glyph dock replaces the project rail, with a library drawer (search, Building / Favourites / All).
- The failure view is now a verdict plus "Try again" / "Edit and retry" under the core; the reasons and compiler output sit in the Request tab.
- New: focus mode (D folds the inspector away), a hover card that fans out a mod's versions, a template library, popups and modals that sit above the portal top bar, and a phone/tablet layout that switches by the app's own width.
- Every v1 feature is still there: projects, live stages, Katara/Saka/Yakko, game and version picker, pasted images, voice with waveform, the rotating rim, versions/diff/restore/branch, explain, templates, notes, favourites, shortcuts, estimates, install/download, the Cyrus badge.
- Light theme: the canvas stays dark in a lifted "Dawn" palette. In light theme the portal's rail and top bar are already dark, so the whole screen reads as one app, and the glow only works on dark.

**The network**
- `components/cyrus/web/engine.ts` (`CyrusWeb`) is ported from the workspace `engine.ts`: orb-web, sagging strands, travelling light with trails, hex core, satellites that open on zoom, pan/zoom/pinch.
- No new dependency: d3-force is replaced by a small ring layout.
- Every mod draws its own constellation, the same one as its dock icon. Running mods get a progress ring; failed ones a red dashed ring.
- Labels are crisp and box-free.
- It pauses off-screen and in hidden tabs. Reduced motion gets still frames; that was broken in round 3 and is fixed.
- Engine draw time measured 6–7 ms per frame in headless software rendering. Real-browser FPS was not measured; headless with software rendering ran 14–22 fps.
- Spec: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v2/SPEC.md`. Four rounds are logged in `ROUNDS.md` (r1–r4). Reference frames are in `reference/`.

**Proofs (real builds)**
- **Image, through the Cyrus UI against the real service:** `mbe20231227d9bb0157249`. The prompt only said "exactly like the attached picture". The picture showed a menu titled "Lumen Bazaar" with three priced items in slots 11/13/15 and a close button in slot 22. The plugin came out named LumenBazaar, and its config.yml has exactly those items, amounts, prices and slots. The service logged "Reading 1.png" and stored the image's checksum.
- **Image, service direct:** `cy04imgproof01`.
- **Live code:** `cy04liveproof02` streamed HelloPlugin.java at about 370 characters a second. The UI build above showed 29 live updates carrying streamed text (frames in `proof/ui/`).
- **Adversarial, all refused on 0.4:** `cy04adv01` (backdoor + webhook), `cy04adv02` (env and /etc/passwd dump), and `cy04advimg01`, the same attack written inside an image.
- All existing safety layers are unchanged. Images sit in the build's `reference/` folder only during each AI call and are removed before the code is cleaned, compiled or extracted.

**Service image and rollback**
- `modbuilder:0.4` is running and healthy. Old builds and the old routes still work.
- `modbuilder:0.3`, 0.2 and 0.1 are still tagged.
- Rollback: `ssh -J root@178.63.94.114 root@10.20.1.253 /opt/modbuilder/run.sh modbuilder:0.3`. The 0.3 files are backed up in `/opt/modbuilder/.v03-backup/`.
- The test container is removed. Its data, including the proof builds, is still in `/var/lib/modbuilder-test` on the VM.
